column1: # AI-slop patterns checked by tools/slop_scan.py and tests/test_prose.py.
# One per line: name<TAB>Python regex (case-insensitive)<TAB>what to write instead.
# Text inside "quotes", `code` and [link text](url) is skipped, so a source's own
# words never trip a pattern. Add a line whenever review finds a slop sentence
# the scanner missed, with the date and the file it came from in the name.

column2: \b(which (its|the|their) (post|blog|report|article) promotes|markets itself as|commercial interest|has a product to sell)\b
column3: Cut it. Say what the source found and link it. A source's business is not a fact about the incident.

column2: \b(draws? on each other|draw on the same|cite each other)\b
column3: Cut it, or name the one shared primary source and link it.

column2: \b(this is this file's|this file's (note|reading|inference|view)|not the sources')
column3: State the fact. If it is inferred, write "No source says X" or "inferred from Y".

column2: \b(worth noting|it'?s important to note|it is important to note|notably,|interestingly,)
column3: Cut the opener and state the fact.

column2: \b(underscores (the|that|how|a|an|its|why)|underscoring|highlights the need|serves as a reminder|stark reminder|sheds light)\b
column3: Cut it. State the fact the sentence is propping up.
Use the concrete property, or cut it.
Say the second thing on its own.

column2: \b(the lesson (here )?is|the takeaway is|key takeaways?|in conclusion|the bottom line)\b
column3: Cut it. End on the last fact or action.
